questions.q: In ETL, where does the transformation step happen?
options: In a separate staging area or dedicated engine, before the data is loaded into the warehouse
Inside the warehouse, after loading
It never happens in ETL
On the source system itself, before extraction
questions.explain: ETL transforms data before it ever reaches the warehouse, so the warehouse only receives clean, finished data.

questions.q: In ELT, where does the transformation step happen?
options: Inside the target system, after the raw data has already been loaded
Before extraction, on the source system
In a completely separate database with no connection to the target
ELT never transforms data at all
questions.explain: ELT loads raw data first, then transforms it using the destination's own compute power.

questions.q: Why can T-SQL itself act as the transformation engine in an ELT pipeline?
options: Because the transformation happens inside the destination database, an INSERT...SELECT with joins and computed columns can perform the transformation directly
T-SQL cannot perform transformations under any circumstances
ELT requires a completely separate programming language
T-SQL can only be used for the extract step, never load or transform
questions.explain: Once raw data is loaded, an ordinary T-SQL statement joining staged data against dimension tables IS the transform step.

questions.q: In the lesson's real transformation example, what does joining staged SalesOrderDetail data against DimProduct and DimDate accomplish?
options: It translates source system keys (ProductID, OrderDate) into the warehouse's own dimension keys, and computes derived columns like SalesAmount
It deletes all rows that don't match any dimension
It converts the fact table into a dimension table
It simply copies data with no changes at all
questions.explain: This is exactly what a transform step does: mapping and computing values so raw source data fits the warehouse's structure.

questions.q: Why do modern cloud warehouses often lean toward ELT rather than ETL?
options: Their compute is cheap and scales well, making it simpler to load raw data first and transform afterward rather than maintain separate transformation tooling
ELT is required by law for any warehouse hosted in the cloud
ETL has been completely removed from all modern database software
ELT uses no compute resources at all
questions.explain: Cheap, scalable destination compute makes doing the transform in-place attractive compared to a separate transformation engine.
